card.name: Spot right before the word among
card.fires_on: The last word or comma of a clause just before 'among' or 'among other things' is expected, often after an adverb or a comparison word such as 'intensively' or 'more frequently'.

modes.label: Adverb before among
modes.description: An adverb ending a verb phrase, with 'among' (a group) coming next.
modes.example: the Church has grown both extensively and intens<<ively>> among English-speaking peoples.

modes.label: Comma before among other things
modes.description: A comma after a clause, where 'among other things' is likely to follow.
modes.example: Holder is under fire<<,>> among other things, for the Justice Department

modes.label: Rate words before a group comparison
modes.description: A word about frequency or risk that is followed by a comparison across groups.
modes.example: Sulfite sensitivity is seen more<< frequently>> in asthmatic than in nonast

card.writes: It pushes the model to predict 'among' (and its Chinese and Russian equivalents) as the next word.
card.plain: It lights up where the text is about to say 'among' a group of people or things.
